The final letter is a tall t with a crossing stroke; it is not a looped d. The joined initial s-t shape and the compressed intervening letters remain consistent with the literal spelling standart.
Between Pour and alpha the page has one mathematical quantifier glyph, with the descending/returning sides and transverse stroke, rather than the four letters of tout.

The long word has compressed ensem strokes followed by the two tall b/l ascenders and a final e. Those ascenders, the longer middle group and the absence of a terminal t support ensemble rather than élément. The initial l and apostrophe are crowded but belong to the same word.

The faint number has a slanted-entry 1 followed by a 7 with a top stroke, descending stem and transverse bar. It is distinct from the dark head number 8 and is assigned to unidentified hand (light pagination).

The cancelled original has a horizontal top bar and descending stem identifiable through the zigzag; the same capital Gamma stands plainly in (18). The number, equals sign, Aut and G are unchanged. Resolves C certainty only; H already reads Gamma.

notes: The page describes geometric fibres as fibres of a scheme of maquettes or MD-graphs, locally isomorphic to a specified graph G. Its data include the underlined vertex and arc schemes, an involution, the marked-point scheme, incidence maps and an inserted weight map to N over the base. It defines a G-épinglage as an isomorphism from the constant graph G over the base to the family graph. With Gamma = Aut G, such markings correspond to sections of a Gamma-torsor, called the torsor of G-épinglages. The final paragraph fixes a base and begins describing the category of G-marked standard curves, introducing hat I_alpha as the disjoint union of I_alpha and tilde A_alpha with cardinality the total weight. This summarizes the manuscript; it is not an independent mathematical verification.

M0940 remains unresolved. The apparent letter after sur cannot be separated securely from the long g-descender of graphes in the inserted parenthesis above. Clear instances of the base letter elsewhere do not justify supplying an independent character here. The original mathcalS|S alternatives are retained in place, with the overlap problem stated explicitly.

The independent base-letter occurrences use a curled form, contrasting with the plain vertex S in the tuple and in alpha in S. In particular, the target of the inserted map, inserted de S, and the G and Gamma subscripts are read with mathcal S. These readings do not resolve the disputed top overlap.

The initial cancelled tuple symbol remains underlined G or underlined S, and the cancelled Le remains doubtful. The cancelled Gamma is resolved by its visible original bar and stem. The cancelled phrase is narrowed to unsure{qui est le}; its middle letters remain obscured, so it is not made certain.

The terminal es of isomorphes is compressed enough to retain isomorphes|isomorphe. Plural remains the preferred reading, with singular explicitly retained; grammatical agreement does not settle the final s. Fixée, the final t of standart, the literal forall symbol, and l'ensemble are settled on their crops.

The lower G-épinglées has only a returning g descender, not an independent underline. The preceding named torseur des G-épinglages does have a real underline across two lines. Ens. has a genuine point on this sheet; the absence of points in earlier sheets is not imposed here.
H acknowledges the head number 8 in an editorial note, so it is not counted as omitted. The pale footer 17 is preserved and assigned to unidentified hand (light pagination).

Independent audit: all seven token-mismatching boxes were inspected in full. The initial maquettes has joined m humps, and the raised prefix has the multiple uprights of MD. The top base-symbol overlap remains unresolved. Independent curled base-S occurrences are distinguished from plain vertex S throughout the tuple, marking and torsor definitions. The canceled initial tuple symbol, Le and qui est le retain their doubts. The canceled Gamma has a surviving straight upper bar and stem, unlike the rounded G beside it. The inserted category parenthesis ends in iso, without the extra final s seen at scan007. The literal universal quantifier has converging/inverted-A strokes rather than two t stems; the union sign has a projecting lower bar beneath two uprights, retained as amalg. Hats, indices and both complete lower formulas agree. No additional mathematical check was performed.
